frontier_addressed: Ambiguous write-outcome reconciliation for a role-local mutable pointer after the write response is unavailable: distinguish committed intended content, unchanged predecessor, and conflicting third content without blindly repeating the effect.

candidate_mechanism.name: deterministic-effect-id three-way read-at-K reconciliation
rule: Freeze predecessor blob K0 and deterministic effect_id before the conditional write.
If the write response is unavailable or ignored, perform one exact readback of the same pointer.
If canonical readback content exactly equals the intended content (including effect_id), classify COMMITTED_INTENDED and never repeat the effect.
Else if readback blob SHA equals K0, classify UNCHANGED_PREDECESSOR; retry is permitted only with the same deterministic effect_id and the same CAS predecessor after a later invocation.
Else classify CONFLICTING_THIRD_CONTENT; do not repeat or overwrite, preserve the conflict for reconciliation.

transfer_mapping: For scheduled-Chat repository side effects, deterministic intent identity plus conditional mutable pointers can convert an ambiguous transport response into a bounded next-read decision instead of an unsafe blind retry. Immutable effect identity and pointer state remain separate concepts; the pointer is only the reconciliation surface.

supporting_evidence.decision_input: The reconciliation decision was made from the exact post-write fetch, not from the update response's commit/content SHA.

falsifying_evidence: Comparing only effect_id is insufficient; a third payload could reuse the identifier with different canonical content, so committed classification requires full intended-content equality.

A single read-at-K cannot distinguish never-committed from committed-then-reverted A->B->A when the mutable pointer can return to identical predecessor content; content-addressed SHA therefore does not solve ABA.

If a third writer overwrites the intended value before readback, the rule intentionally returns CONFLICTING_THIRD_CONTENT and cannot prove whether the intended value existed transiently. It avoids duplicate replay but does not reconstruct history.

repository_and_external_revisions.repository_surface: GitHub contents API via connected GitHub tool; sequential create/update/fetch only

limitations: Live evidence covers only the committed-intended branch on one disposable role-local pointer under sequential execution. The unchanged-predecessor and conflicting-third branches were pure local decision-table checks. No simultaneous writers, network-level ambiguous commit injection, cross-backend semantics, or ABA history were tested.

phase1_constraints.qualification: Only recurring Chat plus lightweight repository transport and local deterministic checking were used; no hosted runner, Codespaces, artifact/LFS/package service, cloud compute, external paid model/API credit, protected authority, or manual user execution is required by the tested mechanism.

conflict_check: Used only frozen sanitized root/control files, own cross_field LATEST/state, own role-local probe/checkpoint, and local deterministic validation. No O/O-derived, other-worker, downstream, legacy, shared-ledger content, other-role receipt, or scheduler semantics were consumed.
candidate_revision: Promote the narrow sequential ambiguous-outcome claim: exact full-content readback plus deterministic effect identity can safely classify committed-intended versus unchanged-predecessor versus conflict without blind replay. Do not promote to history-sensitive exactly-once semantics until ABA is separately handled.
next_exact_test: Falsify ABA resistance on a disposable role-local pointer by constructing A->B->A with the same predecessor content/SHA and test a generation/fencing-token extension that prevents an old read-at-K decision from treating the reverted A as never changed.
continuation: Next invocation bootstrap current manifest/RUN_LIFECYCLE/DESIRED_STATE/cross_field config, freeze authority, reconstruct r182 from LATEST/checkpoint, and execute exactly one bounded child: the separate ABA-resistance leaf on a disposable role-local pointer. Preserve strict canonical-input normalization as a later frontier child and do not repeat the ambiguous-outcome probe.
ledger_note: No automation_control/ledger.jsonl append was attempted because the available update primitive requires reading/replacing the shared ledger content, which is a forbidden semantic input for CLEAN cross_field. The role-local checkpoint and LATEST pointer are the durable authorized evidence surfaces.
